description: v2.1.0 section 14 — Completion as an orthogonal runtime axis. Attaches to an OffenseDef and declares, per form, what extra condition (beyond the base offense's own elements) that form requires and whether/how it is punishable. Section 14.2's OffenseFormInstance<offense, form> is produced by combining this policy with case assessments at runtime (step 7, later) — this schema only covers the definition-time policy, not the runtime resolution.

forms.description: Section 14.1 lists these five forms without per-form field detail beyond 'punishability와 필요한 legal conditions를 정의한다' — each present key opts that form in for this offense; a form key that is absent is simply not available (e.g. an offense with no attempt-punishment provision omits 'attempt' entirely, rather than including it with punishable:false).

requires.description: Extra condition specific to this form (e.g. attempt requires an 실행의 착수 predicate), evaluated in addition to — never instead of — the base offense elements that remain relevant to this form. Section 14 explicitly rejects the 'completed offense failed -> attach attempt label' pattern; this field is what a real attempt-specific requirement (not a base-elements fallback) looks like.

punishability_note.description: Free text for now. Open Question #5 (v2.1.0 section 25) — how far sentencing/punishment modification goes is undecided; this is a placeholder, not a typed effect.
